::: {#thm-union-bound}
#### Union bound

For any events $A_1, \ldots, A_k$, the probability of their union is at most the sum of their probabilities:

$$\Prf{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_k} \le \Pr(A_1) + \cdots + \Pr(A_k).$$
:::

::: proof

The inequality in the second line is @lem-indicator-union.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Prf{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_k}
&= \E{\indic{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_k}}
&& \text{(the expected value of an indicator is the probability of its event)}\\
&\le \E{\indic{A_1} + \cdots + \indic{A_k}}
&& \text{(indicator inequality, and expectation preserves inequalities)}\\
&= \E{\indic{A_1}} + \cdots + \E{\indic{A_k}}
&& \text{(expectation of a sum is the sum of expectations)}\\
&= \Pr(A_1) + \cdots + \Pr(A_k)
&& \text{(the expected value of an indicator is the probability of its event)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-union-bound}
#### The union bound for tests of true null hypotheses

Let $A_j$ be the event that the $j$th of $m$ tests of true null hypotheses, each at level $\siglevel = 0.05$, rejects.
The union bound gives $\Prf{A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_m} \le m \times 0.05$,
which for $m = 10$ is `r 10 * 0.05`.
The exact probability for independent tests is $1 - 0.95^{10} =$ `r round(1 - 0.95^10, 3)`
(@thm-false-positive-prob),
so the bound is not tight, but it needs no independence.
For large $m$ the bound exceeds 1 and says nothing.
:::
